t: Vegas Golden Knights join the NHL
c: In 2017, the league began its second century and expanded again to Las Vegas, Nevada, with the Vegas Golden Knights.

t: Seattle Kraken approved for NHL
c: In 2018, the league approved another expansion team in Seattle, Washington, the Seattle Kraken, which began play in 2021.

t: West Indies wins second Cricket World Cup

t: Australia wins Cricket World Cup
c: 1987 – Australia win the Cricket World Cup, beating England by 7 runs.

c: The codes were drawn up by the so-called "Star and Garter Club" whose members ultimately founded the Marylebone Cricket Club at Lord's in 1787.

t: Broadhalfpenny Down last used by Hambledon
c: Broadhalfpenny Down continued in regular use by Hambledon/Hampshire teams until 1781.

t: Inaugural Test matches played in Australia
c: In 1877, an England touring team in Australia played two matches against full Australian XIs that are now regarded as the inaugural Test matches.

t: The Ashes established after Australian victory

t: South Africa becomes third Test nation

t: Imperial Cricket Conference founded
c: The Imperial Cricket Conference (ICC) was founded in 1909 with England, Australia and South Africa as the founding members.

t: New Zealand and West Indies admitted to Test cricket
c: In 1926, both New Zealand and the West Indies were admitted as members, allowing them to play Test cricket against the other teams.

t: Pakistan becomes Test playing nation
c: New Zealand and India both became Test playing nations before World War II and Pakistan joined soon afterwards in 1952.

t: ICC renames itself International Cricket Council
c: In 1989 the ICC renamed itself the International Cricket Council.

t: London versus Mitcham at Lamb's Conduit Field
c: 1701 to 1720 – There was a London versus Mitcham match in 1707 at Lamb's Conduit Field, Holborn; the result is unknown.

t: Croydon plays London twice in cricket matches
c: 1701 to 1720 – Croydon played London twice in July 1707: the first game was in Croydon, probably at Duppas Hill, and the second at Lamb's Conduit Field.

t: Thomas Marchant first mentions cricket in diary
c: 1701 to 1720 – On Friday, 31 May 1717 Old Style, Thomas Marchant, a farmer from Hurstpierpoint in Sussex, first mentioned cricket in his diary.

t: John Derrick plays cricket as a boy
c: John Derrick, a coroner, testified that he had played cricket on the land when he was a boy in about 1550.

t: John Bullokar describes cricket as game
c: In 1616, John Bullokar referred to cricket in his An English Expositor as "a kind of game with a ball".

t: Oliver Cromwell recorded playing cricket
c: In 1617, the 18-year-old Oliver Cromwell is recorded as playing cricket and football in London.

t: Boxgrove parishioners prosecuted for Sunday cricket
c: In 1622, several parishioners of Boxgrove, near Chichester, were prosecuted for playing cricket in a churchyard on Sunday, 5 May.

t: Ecclesiastical case over East Lavant Sunday cricket
c: In 1628, an ecclesiastical case related to a game at East Lavant, also near Chichester, being played on a Sunday.

t: Long Parliament bans theatres during Civil War
c: When the Civil War began in 1642, the Long Parliament banned theatres, which had met with Puritan disapproval.

t: Three men prosecuted for Eltham Sunday cricket
c: In 1654, three men were prosecuted at Eltham in Kent for playing cricket on a Sunday.

t: Edward Bound exonerated for playing cricket

t: Death following cricket match at Horsted Keynes
c: In 1624, a fatality occurred following a match on 28 August Old Style (7 September New Style), at Horsted Keynes in Sussex.

t: Five-a-side matches between Richmond and London

t: London plays Essex and Hertfordshire combined team
c: 1731–1740 – London continued to play against county opposition and, for many years, there were few inter-county matches.

t: Surrey plays multiple matches against rival counties
c: 1731–1740 – Surrey were prominent in 1736, playing four matches against Middlesex, three against London, and two against Kent.

t: Essex plays London in first named matches
c: 1731–1740 – In 1737, Essex played London twice.

t: Earliest known tie in eleven-a-side match
c: 1741–1750 – The earliest known tie in an eleven-a-side match occurred on 22 July 1741, when Surrey played London on Richmond Green.

t: Cricket established as common at Eton College
c: In 1727, Horace Walpole commented that it was already "common" at Eton College—the earliest reference to it both at Eton and in the county of Berkshire.

t: John Frame began cricket career
c: There was also John Frame, only 16 when his career began in 1749, who went on to become one of the first great fast bowlers.

t: London versus Dartford cricket rivalry begins
c: Matches between London and Dartford were first recorded in 1722, and this rivalry, albeit sporadic, continued into the 1750s.

t: Hampshire and Sussex appear in team titles
c: They met twice in 1729, with the first match in Dartford being played for a stake of £50, but the result is unknown.

c: Laleham Burway was first recorded as the venue for two Chertsey matches in 1736.

c: In 1737, he arranged three matches there in which the Prince of Wales' XI met Sir William Gage's XI, the 3rd Duke of Marlborough's XI, and London.

t: Richmond organises matches against Alan Brodrick
c: In 1727, the 2nd Duke of Richmond organised two matches between his own team and Alan Brodrick's XI.

t: Pitch length standardised at 23 yards
c: The only early rule about pitch and wicket dimensions was re the length of the pitch at 23 yards in 1727; this had become a chain (22 yards) by 1744.

t: Kent plays England before crowd of ten thousand
c: In 1739, the return match between Kent and England was played on the Artillery Ground before a crowd of over 10,000.

t: Earliest references to cricket patrons
c: 1768 marks the earliest references to patrons John Sackville, 3rd Duke of Dorset, and Sir Horatio Mann in a cricketing context.

t: Laws of Cricket re-codified with leg before wicket
c: The Laws of Cricket underwent a re-codification in 1775, including the introduction of the leg before wicket rule.

t: Cricket documented in Durham, Somerset, Warwickshire, Yorkshire
c: The earliest references to cricket in the counties of Durham, Somerset, Warwickshire and Yorkshire all occurred in 1751.

t: Leeds and Sheffield clubs played
c: Five eleven-a-side matches were recorded in 1765, including two in Yorkshire between the Leeds and Sheffield clubs.
